Delivery Confirmation

Formal acknowledgment, either digital or physical, that goods have been delivered to and accepted by the consignee, as evidenced in official transport documentation.

Quick answer: Formal acknowledgment, either digital or physical, that goods have been delivered to and accepted by the consignee, as evidenced in official transport documentation.

Quick answer

Formal acknowledgment, either digital or physical, that goods have been delivered to and accepted by the consignee, as evidenced in official transport documentation.

Why it matters

Delivery Confirmation matters because it supports clear communication in Visibility and Tracking contexts for Freight Forwarders, Supply Chain Managers, and Customs Brokers. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as FIATA Diploma, CILT Certification, and IATA DGR.

Questions and answers

Questions and answers

What is Delivery Confirmation?

In this glossary, Delivery Confirmation refers to: Formal acknowledgment, either digital or physical, that goods have been delivered to and accepted by the consignee, as evidenced in official transport documentation.

How is Delivery Confirmation used in logistics?

In logistics communication, this term appears in contexts such as: "Delivery confirmation must be submitted to the carrier within 24 hours of receipt, as stated in the bill of lading terms."

Why does Delivery Confirmation matter in logistics?

Delivery Confirmation matters because it supports clear communication in Visibility and Tracking contexts for Freight Forwarders, Supply Chain Managers, and Customs Brokers. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as FIATA Diploma, CILT Certification, and IATA DGR.

Who uses Delivery Confirmation?

Delivery Confirmation is mainly used by Freight Forwarders, Supply Chain Managers, and Customs Brokers.

What category does Delivery Confirmation belong to?

In this glossary, Delivery Confirmation is grouped under Visibility and Tracking. Related pages in this category explain adjacent procedures, commands and operational concepts.

Where does this definition come from?

This definition is sourced from Incoterms 2020 (ICC), FIATA, IATA DGR, WCO and published by Protermify Logistics as a static logistics reference page.

Definition

Formal acknowledgment, either digital or physical, that goods have been delivered to and accepted by the consignee, as evidenced in official transport documentation.

Operational example

Delivery confirmation must be submitted to the carrier within 24 hours of receipt, as stated in the bill of lading terms.
